appraisal_events.evidence: Mme de Guermantes avait même mis à exclure Mme et Mlle Swann une persévérance qui avait étonné ... l'élégance est de ne pas connaître Mme Swann. Et la duchesse riait de tout son cœur.
appraisal_events.explanation: The duchess sustains a years-long, extreme refusal to know Swann's wife and daughter, treating it within her circle as a badge of supreme elegance; the narrator's framing of her disproportionate persistence carries a note of irony.

appraisal_events.evidence: Gilberte... ne cessait de penser avec admiration à l'insolente Mme de Guermantes... elle avait voulu écrire à la duchesse pour lui demander ce qu'elle avait contre une jeune fille qui ne lui avait rien fait. Les Guermantes avaient pris à ses yeux des proportions que leur noblesse eût été impuissante à leur donner.
appraisal_events.explanation: Rather than resenting decades of insults, Gilberte admires the very woman who snubbed her and craves her approval, a psychological subordination the narrator explicitly analyzes as contrary to what common sense would expect.

appraisal_events.evidence: Je ne vois aucun inconvénient à ce que nous connaissions cette petite... Tout le monde sait que nous aimions beaucoup Swann. On trouvera cela tout naturel.
appraisal_events.explanation: After decades of exclusion, the duchess casually and definitively agrees to receive Gilberte, closing the boundary that had kept her out of the Guermantes circle.

status_effects.explanation: She and her mother are kept outside the duchess's circle with exceptional, prideful persistence, held up within that circle as proof of its exclusivity.
Her refusal to know Mme Swann is cited approvingly within her own set (Bébel's remark) as the very definition of elegance, a witnessed boost to her standing even as the narrator frames it ironically.
She remains emotionally dependent on and admiring of the woman who wronged her rather than claiming any advantage from the eventual reversal, a position of continued subordination.
The long-standing boundary against her is finally and explicitly lifted, a distinct, later moment of the passage separate from the sustained exclusion of E1.

ambiguities: The duchess's motives for softening are left genuinely mixed (residual affection for the dead Swann, curiosity, pride in her own magnanimity, social convenience), so E3 is read as a clear local inclusion for Gilberte without attributing a single settled motive to the duchess.
